title: DriftEvent
description: One entry in Compare-EntraPostureConditionalAccessDrift's own DriftEvents array (VNext build order item 10, drift detection). Implements the review plan's own drift categories (WS4 task 12: policy added/removed/changed, effective coverage changed, expected case changed, object scope changed) and its own drift definition: 'a snapshot change identifies the fact, affected control/case, and old/new result.' 'Effective coverage changed' is answered via relatedResultTransitions, not a separate category here -- it is exactly what the pre-existing comparison ResultTransitions already computes. 'Object scope changed' is the isScopeChange flag on a PolicyModified event, not its own top-level category.

driftEventId.description: Deterministic, not random -- '<category>::<entityId>' -- so re-running the same comparison twice against the same two snapshots produces identical IDs.

entityType.description: 'ConditionalAccessPolicy' for policy-level events, or the synthetic type 'CA-002-Scenario' for expected-case events (entityId is a scope key, not a real evidence entity, in that case).

entityId.description: The policy's entityId for policy-level events, or the CA-002 scope key (role::platform::clientAppType::locationTrust::signInRisk::userRisk) for expected-case events.

isScopeChange.description: True when a PolicyModified event's fieldChanges include at least one conditions.users.* path. Null for every other category, where the concept doesn't apply -- explicit null, not omitted, per this project's own missing-vs-null discipline.

fieldChanges.description: Populated only for PolicyModified; empty for every other category.

affectedControlIds.description: CA-001 and CA-002 for policy-level events (either could plausibly be affected by any policy change); CA-002 only for expected-case events, since CA-001's own scenario grid is a fixed constant that never drifts.

relatedResultTransitions.description: The subset of the comparison's own ResultTransitions this drift event plausibly explains, correlated by EvidenceReferences (policy-level events) or Scope (expected-case events) -- answers the review plan's own 'affected control/case, and old/new result' requirement directly. Can be empty even for a real drift event, e.g. a policy change whose affected scenarios did not happen to change status.
